land.text: the Bahmani province (taraf) of Berar, divided in 1478 or 1479 into the provinces of Gawil and Mahur, which Fathullah Imad-ul-Mulk reunited under Ellichpur

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Bahmani row ends 1491 and the five Deccan sultanates begin 1492; the Berar page dates the independence to 1490.

land.text: Berar, annexed 'into his own dominions of the Ahmadnagar Sultanate in 1574' by Murtaza Nizam Shah I

successors.note: Cliopatria keeps the Berar row to 1578 and gives the land to Ahmadnagar from 1579; the page's year is 1574.

capitals.name: Ellichpur (Achalpur)
capitals.note: The infobox gives 'Capital: Ellichpur'; Gavilgad and Narnala were fortified as strongholds. Coordinates are those of modern Achalpur.

rulers.name: Fathullah Imad-ul-Mulk
rulers.note: The page's text prints his death as '150,4'; the reign table gives 1490-1504.

rulers.name: Darya Imad Shah
rulers.note: The text says he 'ascended the throne in 1530', the table 1529.

rulers.name: Burhan Imad Shah
rulers.note: Table: 'de facto 1562-1568'; deposed by his regent and minister Tufail Khan, then put to death by Murtaza Nizam Shah I.

correction.text: the same shape as Cliopatria's 1492-1518 row, drawn from the 1490 independence: Berar with Mahur annexed, the capital at Ellichpur, Gavilgad and Narnala fortified

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the page dates independence to 1490 ('In 1490, Fathullah Imad-ul-Mulk... proclaimed his independence amidst the civil unrest in the Bahmani Sultanate'; the Bahmani page names the 1490 revolts of Yusuf Adil Shah, Malik Ahmad Nizam Shah I and Fathullah Imad-ul-Mulk) but Cliopatria starts the row in 1492. Area: the infobox gives 29,340 km2 against Cliopatria's 80,056 km2 (ratio 2.7, beyond a factor of two); the page gives no boundary and the shape covers the northern two thirds of Vidarbha (the gazetteer's Vidarbha is about 122,000 km2), so the infobox figure is read as the core around Ellichpur and Mahur and the shape is kept.

80,056 km2 for 1492-1518, 2.7 times the infobox's 29,340 km2 (see the 1490 keyframe); the page names Berar, Mahur, Ellichpur and Gavilgad and no boundary, so the shape stands as the best available outline of the Bahmani province of Berar.

3 cells (about 750 km2) of the Mahur edge pass to Bidar and Golconda in Cliopatria's 1519 row, when Golconda is born; no page opened dates or names that strip, so no ledger event is written for it (below the resolution of the pages).
A 2-cell revision of the northern edge (about 500 km2) that the page does not mention; shape kept, no event.

correction.text: unchanged shape; the years are 1572-1573 only, because Ahmadnagar annexed Berar in 1574

keyframe_review.note: The shape is right but ends four years late: 'Murtaza Nizam Shah... proceeded to annex Berar into his own dominions of the Ahmadnagar Sultanate in 1574' and the infobox gives 'Conquered by the Ahmednagar Sultanate: 1574'. Cliopatria runs the row to 1578 and starts Ahmadnagar's enlarged shape in 1579; the shape holds 1572-1573 only.

region.text: Berar with Mahur annexed, capital Ellichpur; Gavilgad and Narnala fortified

ledger.note: 1490: Fathullah Imad-ul-Mulk proclaims the independence of Berar from the Bahmani Sultanate at Ellichpur. 'In 1490, Fathullah Imad-ul-Mulk... proclaimed his independence amidst the civil unrest in the Bahmani Sultanate. He proceeded to annex Mahur to his new kingdom and had its capital at Ellichpur'; Gavilgad and Narnala 'were also fortified by him'. The Bahmani page lists the 1490 revolt of Fathullah Imad-ul-Mulk.

region.text: all of Berar, from Ellichpur to Mahur

ledger.note: 1574: Ahmadnagar annexes Berar. Murtaza Nizam Shah I 'invaded Berar, imprisoned and put to death Tufail Khan, his son Shams-ul-Mulk, and the former king Burhan' and 'proceeded to annex Berar into his own dominions of the Ahmadnagar Sultanate in 1574' (the Ahmadnagar page agrees: 'annexed Berar in 1574, bringing the sultanate to its territorial zenith'). Cliopatria carries the row to 1578.
1574: the Imad Shahi sultanate ends; its land becomes part of the Ahmadnagar Sultanate. Infobox: 'Conquered by the Ahmednagar Sultanate: 1574'.

wars.name: Ahmadnagar's annexation of Berar

zones.text: Berar, annexed by Murtaza Nizam Shah I in 1574

wars.outcome: Ahmadnagar victory: the regent Tufail Khan and the deposed king Burhan Imad Shah are put to death and Berar is absorbed into the Ahmadnagar Sultanate.
wars.note: The page gives the usurpation of Tufail Khan (1568) and the annexation (1574) but no campaign dates before 1574; earlier it says Berar 'resisted the aggression of Ahmadnagar with the help of Bahadur Shah, sultan of Gujarat' (undated) and that Darya Imad Shah tried to align with Bijapur in 1530 'but was unsuccessful'.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary survey or treaty line for Berar; the frontiers with Khandesh, Ahmadnagar and Bidar are Cliopatria's approximations.

sources.title: Berar Sultanate
sources.note: Identity, independence 1490, Ellichpur, rulers, the 1574 annexation by Ahmadnagar, infobox area 29,340 km2.

sources.title: Bahmani Sultanate
sources.note: The 1490 revolts and the break-up of the Bahmani Sultanate into five states after 1518 (context for the predecessor).

sources.title: Battle of Talikota
sources.note: Talikota page: 'the Berar Sultanate did not join the battle' (its infobox lists Berar); used for the note only.

notes: Berar (4 Cliopatria shapes, 1492-1578): the page gives only the annexation date (1574), so Cliopatria's 1575-1578 years are wrong and 1579 is when Ahmadnagar's enlarged shape begins. Infobox area (29,340 km2) is 2.7 times smaller than the shape (80,056 km2); the page names no boundary. Two 2-3 cell revisions (1519, 1564) are boundary noise and have no ledger event. The Battle of Talikota page says 'the Berar Sultanate did not join the battle' although its infobox lists Berar; no war entry was written for it. The page mentions Gujarat's help against Ahmadnagar (Bahadur Shah) without a date. Khandesh (Berar's northern neighbour) has no Cliopatria row; if sa-04-x adds it, the 1519-1572 northern edge of Berar can be checked against it.
